fixes.explanation: Right, friend. Jesus says, “And whoever sees Me sees the One who sent Me.” (John 12:45) Just before this, He said that believing in Him means believing in the One who sent Him (John 12:44). So looking at Jesus doesn't stop at Jesus. The One being seen is the Father who sent Him (John 12:49), and that's who a person is looking at when they see Jesus.

That's a fair guess, but it's not the word Jesus uses. He says, “For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.” (John 12:47) Right before that, He said He has come as a light so that no one who believes in Him should remain in darkness (John 12:46). Bringing people out of the dark is saving, not testing, so the blank is save.

Rule makes sense as a guess, but Jesus doesn't use it. He says, “For I have not come to judge the world, but to save the world.” (John 12:47) Right before that, He said He has come as a light so that no one who believes in Him should remain in darkness (John 12:46). That's a light for people in the dark, not a ruler taking charge, so the blank is save.

problems.problem: It still does not explain what seeing the One who sent Jesus means; it only says that seeing Jesus reaches Him.
It still repeats the contrast between judging and saving without explaining it.
It still repeats the contrast without explaining how it clarifies the choice.
